doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Loneliness of a Long Distance Runner, his composed soprano record
summary: Inspired by the idea of the artist as a marathon runner, he wrote out a heavily composed multi-soprano album around the time he met Caris.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Teo did the editing. An interesting record that’s pretty well known over the years is The Lonliness of a Long Distance Runner, one of your solo records. How’d that come about?

The theme is from the book. The book and the movie had nothing to do with long distance running. But I loved the image of the long distance runner and the idea of the artist as a long distance runner. This was a very programmatic – the race, going against the wall, breakaway, wall of pain. I interviewed runners. I found out what it is like. It’s just the idea of marathon runner. I couldn’t think of anything more out, racing for 26 miles or 26 kilometers, whatever it is. What a fascinating thing. It made me – it really – great images in my mind. That is one of the most composed records I’ve ever
done. Everything is written out. I really worked on that, all soprano. If it wasn’t for Walter Quintus, who got me in tune, it would be unlistenable, Walter the engineer.
So basically, the tunes are all through-composed?

There’s a lot of writing. The book, it’s like this. I wrote a lot. There are four sopranos – sometimes four sopranos, sometimes three. I really put my heart and soul into that record. I was living in Long Island. I was basically on my own, and I could do it. I had the time to do it.
Is this around the time you met your wife, by the way?
Yes, my lovely wife, around that time.
